caption:
Stop reshooting a video just to swap one thing in the shot 🎬

Changing the actor, the location or the product used to mean booking a set again. Higgsfield's new tool Genjutsu takes the video you already have and rebuilds it around a new character, scene or product while the acting, lip sync and camera moves stay exactly the same.

→ Motion Transfer: keep the performance, change who's in it
→ Object Swap: change one thing, keep the rest of the shot
→ Works on 4-30 second clips, output up to 1080p
→ Free to try on Higgsfield

What would you recast first: the actor, the location, or the product? 👇

Follow @aiplaybooks.daily for a new AI tool every day.

Higgsfield's new AI tool Genjutsu lets you swap the actor, the location or the product in a video while keeping the exact same performance — no reshoot needed.

Motion Transfer keeps the acting, lip sync and camera moves, then rebuilds the scene around a new character. Object Swap changes one chosen element and leaves the rest of the shot untouched.

It's free to try, works on reference clips 4 to 30 seconds long, and outputs up to 1080p.

slides.title: Recast any video without reshooting it.
slides.sub: Same acting, same camera moves — Higgsfield's new tool swaps who or what's in the shot.
slides.voiceover: Higgsfield just launched a tool that recasts any video without reshooting it.

slides.label: WHAT GENJUTSU DOES
slides.title: Two modes, one reference video
items: Keeps the motion, camera work and timing, then rebuilds the scene around a new character
Changes one chosen element — a character, outfit, product or location — keeps the rest untouched
Acting, lip sync, camera movement and VFX stay consistent between the original and the new version
Pick a mode, upload your video, choose a preset or add a short description
slides.voiceover: It keeps the acting, lip sync and camera moves, and rebuilds everything else around them.

slides.label: WHAT YOU CAN RECAST
slides.title: Same shot, different world
items: Put a different person or costume into the exact same performance
Keep the acting and camera work, move the whole scene somewhere else
Drop in a different product or wardrobe while the rest of the shot stays the same
slides.voiceover: Swap the character, the location, or just one product in the shot.

slides.label: OLD WAY VS. GENJUTSU
slides.title: What you skip by not reshooting

cols.name: Reshooting a scene
points: Book actors, a set and a crew again
Re-match the exact camera moves by hand
Redo lighting, VFX and edit from scratch

cols.name: Genjutsu
points: Upload the one video you already have
Motion, timing and camera moves carry over
Rebuilds the cast, scene or product around it

slides.voiceover: Reshooting means booking a set again. Genjutsu just rebuilds the shot you already have.

slides.label: HOW TO TRY IT
slides.title: Three steps, no editing experience needed
steps: A reference clip from `4 to 30 seconds` long
Pick Motion Transfer or Object Swap
Add up to 30 reference images of the new character, product or location
Choose a preset or write a short description, then generate the result
slides.voiceover: Upload a clip, pick a mode, add your references, and generate.

slides.label: INPUT LIMITS
slides.title: How long your reference video can be
slides.sub: Genjutsu currently supports reference videos from 4 to 30 seconds, plus up to 30 reference images per run.
slides.voiceover: Reference videos run from four to thirty seconds long.

slides.label: WORTH KNOWING
slides.title: Free to try, credits after that
items: Free to try on Higgsfield; longer runs and higher resolution cost more credits
Only tested on Higgsfield's own Genjutsu tool — results vary by footage
slides.voiceover: It's free to try, and output goes all the way up to 1080p.

slides.title: Reshoots are becoming
slides.voiceover: Reshoots are becoming optional — follow us for more free AI tools like this.
